title: HEAVY RAINS
full_story:
Torrential rainfall Monday caused some flooding problems in Clay County.

At the US Weather Bureau Station at WNOI we recorded 3.25 inches of rain.  Louisville recorded 3.44” of rain, Clay City recorded 1.34”, Iuka recorded 2.43”, while Cisne officially recorded only .39”.  Effingham county recorded 3.5 inches, 2.65” were recorded in Salem, and 2.39 inches was recorded in Centralia.

Steve Lewis with Clay County ESDA reported that he hadn’t received any reports of storm damage.  Just flooding issues.

The National Weather Service has issued a River Flood Warning for the Little Wabash below Clay City.  The river was expected to rise above flood stage last night and is predicted to crest at 22.1’ on Wednesday morning.  Flood Stage is 18 feet.

title: FLORA CITY COUNCIL MEETS
full_story:
The Flora City Council met Monday afternoon and covered many topics before adjourning a short time later.

Mayor Linda Spicer called the meeting to order and then recognized a number of visitors who were seeking to address city government leaders.  The mayor first called on Cindy Leib from First Christian Church of Flora.  She announced that the church is planning a special event to honor America’s 250th Anniversary.  It’s called the Spirit of 1776 and takes place on Flag Day, June 14 around the church property.  She says all Clay County Churches are encouraged to participate and partner with them and the Ministerial Alliance as everyone comes together to celebrate America.  There will be hot dogs, ice cream, food trucks, games, a bounce house, cornhole, a pie-making contest, watermelon seed spitting contest, a costume contest and more.  The event will run from 2:00-6:00pm, with a service starting at 5:00 to honor country and a time for reflection on America and its people.  Lieb stated that part of the planning included cooperation with Flora Police Chief Jeremy Ruger and they asked the city to close the 100 Block of 4th and 5th streets during the event.  A motion was made to approve their request and it passed unanimously.

Next, Heather Greenwood with Flora Rotary briefly addressed commissioners to request the use of the Pickleball Courts for the first ever Rotary Pickleball Tournament, which is hoped to become an annual event.  The tournament, scheduled for June 19 and 20 would feature divisions for women and men singles and doubles and mixed doubles, in categories of 18 and under, open and 55 and over.  Greenwood also stated that they intend to honor the memory of Charlie “Pokie Dot” Workman, a famous local sanitation worker for many years in Flora. He was portrayed during the Rotary’s Cemetery tours several years back.   The plaque will be on display at the new Rotary Bathrooms at the Pickleball Courts.  Commissioners had positive remarks about the tournament and the plaque and approved the request without dissent.

Noelle Fopay was delayed from arriving at the start of the meeting but did make it before the meeting adjourned.  She explained that she has taught yoga for ten years and a group of enthusiasts explained that they get together to practice yoga at various venues around town and especially like to use the gazebo at Charley Brown Park.  Fopay presented documentation and proof of insurance for what they propose, to meet on Thursdays at 6:00pm.  City Clerk Kaci O’Dell confirmed the insurance is what the city’s insurer is looking for.  After a question of two, commissioners approved her request.

Mayor Spicer then asked for the meeting agenda and consent to be approved and it was quickly approved.  The latter included past meeting minutes, the warrant list, Treasurer’s Report, Police Activity Report and Building and Zoning Report for April.

In Regular Business, Mayor Spicer thanked everyone who helped put on this past weekend’s Springfest event put on by Flora Tourism.  While there was rain, there were many visitors and there was a BBQ cookoff and the event was labeled a success.  Spicer said that this week, May 18-23, is National Public Works Week, adding that the official theme is “Rooted in Service, Powered by Community.”  She felt that very much describes Flora Public Works.  The mayor then sought to appoint Nikki Green to Flora Tourism Committee to a two-year term ending May 18, 2028 and her nomination was quickly approved on a unanimous vote.

Commissioner Phil Wiley thanked everyone who attended Springfest over the weekend and especially for those who participated in setting it all up and participated including merchants and the competitors for the BBQ Cookoff Contest.  He said it was a very good event.  Wiley also took a moment to remind everyone about practicing safety with the heavy rains that caused widespread flooding.  Don’t drive through flood waters.  Check that sump pumps are working and warned about preparing for flooded basements and moving your belongings and keeping pets safe too.  He added it looks like more inclement weather is headed our way.  Wiley then introduced an ordinance amending Title 8, Chapter 3, Section 4 concerning gas rates.  He said the proposal is to raise Flora’s natural gas rate one percent, something that hasn’t happened for the past 12 years, but the time has come to implement the new rate.  Commissioner Jeremy Henderson noted that the statistics need to be publicly released so people can see why the city is taking action now.  When the measure was brought to a vote, it was approved 4-1, with Jeremy Henderson voting No.  Wiley stated Henderson’s comment about planning for the future is why the action needed to be taken now and the proposal was very fair.

Flora Police Chief Jeremy Ruger asked the council to approve a budgeted item, the purchase of a Flock Safety device to assist in law enforcement and criminal investigations.  He said people think its about license plate readers knowing everyone’s every move, but that is not correct.  It is used in investigations, but it’s also used in situations where someone with dementia can be quickly found as just happened.  Commissioners approved his request at a cost of $10,950.

City Administrator/Economic Development Director Mike Stanford noted that the Safe Routes to School construction was to begin on Monday, but with the heavy rain, there wasn’t much of anything they could do.  But they are poised to get started when conditions are right.  Stanford also said that Flora has learned that its second application for Safe Routes to School Sidewalk Grant was approved for $250,000, but it will be sometime before it is awarded.  He said the sidewalk on Shadwell from the jr. high to Olive St was originally planned for in the 1970’s when the school was built, but was not put in for one reason or another, but will be in the coming weeks.  Also slated for completion are sidewalks on east third street from Stanford Rd to Olive or near Olive, but it’s unclear how soon that will occur.  Stanford also presented a resolution regarding Title 8, Chapter 3, Section 2(J) Water and Sewer Rates.  He proposed to waive the scheduled 2026–2027 3% water rate increase for residential customers located inside the city limits and for all water users with monthly consumption below 250,000 gallons.  The scheduled water rate increase would still apply to customers located outside the city limits, as well as to all customers whose monthly water usage exceeds 250,000 gallons per month.  In place of the water rate increase, the City proposes a 3% increase to sewer rates for all sewer customers, both inside and outside the city limits.

The overall impact of this adjustment will result in a slight cost savings for residential customers located inside the city limits.  For those customers, the net effect will be a decrease of approximately $0.17 per month on the first 1,000 gallons used, and approximately $0.01 savings per each additional 1,000 gallons thereafter.

This adjustment is necessary to more appropriately allocate revenue between the water and sewer departments and to ensure each utility fund remains properly supported based on operational needs and system demands.  The measure was approved unanimously.  Stanford added that Matt Johnson is coming to Flora to update the city on the proposed new sewage treatment plant.  He also briefly conferred with Superintendent of Public Services Toby Rinehart about dealing with infiltration of zinc into the Flora plant and how they are dealing with it.

As the meeting drew to a close, Toby Rinehart asked commissioners to approve the budgeted purchase of components to update the lift station on North Olive on the property of Car Corral at a cost of $38,507 from Vandevanter Engineering.  The measure was approved and the meeting adjourned.

title: FLORA SCHOOL BOARD MEETING
full_story:
The Flora Unit School Board met in regular session last night.  The Board recognized the staff retiring at the end of the school year, the leadership award winners at Floyd Henson Junior High School, and the business students and Mrs. Westjohn from Flora High School for their success at competitions.

The board also approved the Intergovernmental Agreement between the Clay County Health Department and the district for the Prevention Initiative Birth to Three Program for the 2026-2027 school year.

In personnel matters the board employed Jessica Holloway as guidance counselor at Floyd Henson Junior High School and approved Cassy Chapman as a volunteer assistant coach for high school girls’ volleyball, Allie Krutsinger as the high school basketball cheerleading coach, Emily Welty as 7th grade volleyball coach, Owen Leib as Fresh/Soph basketball coach for the next school year.

The board also accepted the resignations of Ben Carril as guidance counselor, Amy Wood as transportation secretary, Christy Rascher as transportation aide, Lindsey Fehrenbacher as Parent Educator, Jamie Oestreich as 8th grade girls’ basketball coach and Jessica Crawford as junior class sponsor.  And the intent to retire submitted by Steve Wilson.

title: FLORA POLICE ACTIVITY REPORT
full_story:
Flora Chief of Jeremy Ruger released his Activity Report for April during Monday’s Flora City Council meeting.

During the month, Flora police officers investigated 5 traffic accidents.

They made 10 criminal arrests.  There were 2 drug arrests and 2 DUI arrests during April.  There were no local ordinance arrests, 18 traffic arrests and 5 warrant arrests.

Officers issued 43 warning tickets, responded to 20 alarms and had 1,040 calls for service and had two juvenile contacts.

Also, Flora police officers drove 7,508 miles and conducted 57 investigations during April.  They answered 299, 911 calls and conducted 14 UTV Inspections and one Golf Cart Inspections during April.

title: FLORA CLEAN-UP DAYS
full_story:
The City of Flora is having town-wide clean-up days this week.

Accumulated, unwanted items at residences will be picked up at no extra charge on the residents normal trash day.  It is requested small or loose items should be bundled or bagged.  Carpet needs to be cut and tied so one person can handle it, broken glass items need to be bagged and marked for safety, multiple items such as brooms, mops, blinds, etc. need to be tied together, pool liners need to be cut down, and metal swing sets need to be broken down.  All mattresses and box springs must be wrapped in plastic, in order to be picked up.

For electronic items such as televisions and monitors, radios, tape recorders, computer hard drives, monitors, printers, cell phones, etc. residents are ask to please contact Secure Processors at 618-662-4823.

Republic Services, Flora’s solid waste hauler, will not accept any white goods such as stoves, dishwashers, washing machines, clothes dryers, etc., tires or vehicle/boat parts, paint, hazardous materials/waste, landscape waste, construction/remodeling/demolition materials, concrete/brick/asphalt, batteries, pressurized tanks, gas/oil/antifreeze, ammunition, or explosives.

Residents may deliver their properly decommissioned, no Freon or Oil, white goods to Public Works West lot at 200 Fairview Street.  Please follow the signs posted.  This will be a residential only pick up site.  The city will only be accepting white goods daily between the hours of 7:30 am to 3:30 pm.

Please keep weight in mind when grouping items, such as books and magazines, in a bag or trash container.

Residents with any further questions should call 618-662-4625 or email [email protected].

title: FLORA BUILDING AND ZONING REPORT
full_story:
Flora Building and Zoning Official Chad Bayles presented the monthly building and zoning report for April during Monday’s Flora City Council meeting.

The report shows 11 new residential construction projects were undertaken in April, valued at $273,919.

There were 3 new commercial projects that started during April, valued at $17,404,334.

And there were no new industrial projects started during April.

There were 14 total new projects in Flora for April, valued at $17,678,253 with $1,210 collected in permit fees and $350 in deposit fees for April

The year-to-date figures show 29 total residential projects so far this year with a value of $428,783.

There are four year-to-date commercial projects valued at $17,444,334 and no new industrial projects.

That makes 33 total projects valued at $17,873,117, with $1,933 in permit fees and $550 in deposit fees collected for the year.
